LESSON: CONVERSATIONAL SKILLS: INTERVIEWS

Grade: Grade 8
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 6
Topic 11.1.1: Conversational Skills: interviews

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Conversational Skills: interviews. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Which words or phrases are used to show politeness?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. use conversational strategies to disagree appropriately
2. apply non-verbal cues to express varied moods and feelings

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: CONVERSATIONAL SKILLS: INTERVIEWS
Subject: ENGLISH · Grade: Grade 8
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Conversational Skills: interviews helps you succeed in ENGLISH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: CONVERSATIONAL SKILLS: INTERVIEWS
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Use conversational strategies to disagree appropriately

What this means
In this part you learn to use conversational strategies to disagree appropriately. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: use conversational strategies to disagree appropriately.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Conversational Skills: interviews”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can use conversational strategies to disagree appropriately. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Apply non-verbal cues to express varied moods and feelings

What this means
In this part you learn to apply non-verbal cues to express varied moods and feelings. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: apply non-verbal cues to express varied moods and feelings.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Conversational Skills: interviews to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can apply non-verbal cues to express varied moods and feelings. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Conversational Skills: interviews is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Conversational Skills: interviews”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: use conversational strategies to disagree appropriately)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Conversational Skills: interviews to a partner. (skill: apply non-verbal cues to express varied moods and feelings)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Conversational Skills: interviews to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: use conversational strategies to disagree appropriately.
3. Practise this skill: apply non-verbal cues to express varied moods and feelings.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Conversational Skills: interviews from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Conversational Skills: interviews: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 8 learner study Conversational Skills: interviews?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which words or phrases are used to show politeness?
2. How do you use non-verbal cues to express different moods and feelings?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Conversational Skills: interviews means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: use conversational strategies to disagree appropriately.
5. Be able to: apply non-verbal cues to express varied moods and feelings.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
